subsystems.name: Panel
subsystems.role: the light valve or light emitter that forms the image pixel by pixel.

subsystems.name: Backlight (LCD only)
subsystems.role: provides the white light that the liquid crystal layer modulates.

subsystems.name: Driver electronics
subsystems.role: addresses each pixel row by row and sets the voltage or current that defines its brightness.

subsystems.name: Scaler and interface board
subsystems.role: receives video from the computer, scales and processes it, and sends it to the panel.

subsystems.name: Power supply
subsystems.role: converts mains AC into the DC rails used by the panel, backlight and electronics.

subsystems.name: Chassis and stand
subsystems.role: holds the panel rigid and flat, and provides mounting and ergonomic adjustment.
parts: stand with tilt, swivel and height adjustment

buildSteps.title: Pattern the transistor array
buildSteps.detail: On large glass sheets, thin-film transistor layers are deposited and etched by photolithography so that every pixel has its own switch. Silicon, or faster indium-gallium-zinc-oxide for high refresh rates, is used.

buildSteps.title: Form colour filters
buildSteps.detail: Red, green and blue resin patterns and a black matrix are deposited on the opposite glass plate, one set per pixel.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the LCD cell
buildSteps.detail: The two glass plates are aligned, sealed around the edge, and the gap is filled with liquid crystal. Polarizing films are laminated to the outside. For OLED, organic layers are deposited on the transistor backplane instead and sealed against moisture.

buildSteps.title: Build the backlight
buildSteps.detail: LED strips are mounted along an edge or across the back. A light guide, diffuser and prism films spread the light evenly. This step is omitted for OLED, which emits its own light.

buildSteps.title: Bond drivers and flexible circuits
buildSteps.detail: Gate and source driver chips are attached along the panel edges, and flexible printed circuits connect them to the control boards.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The scaler board, power supply and input ports are screwed into the rear housing and connected to the panel.

buildSteps.title: Final assembly and calibration
buildSteps.detail: The panel is fitted into the bezel, the stand is attached, and colour, gamma and brightness uniformity are measured and corrected before testing and packing.

prerequisites.why: every pixel needs a switch for fast, uniform control.
they form the light valve in the dominant LCD technology.
they set brightness and contrast for LCD screens.
organic layers give perfect blacks but must be sealed from moisture and are harder to make on large sheets.
HDMI, DisplayPort and USB-C carry the increasing data rates of high resolution and high refresh.
sRGB, DCI-P3 and HDR formats let content and monitors agree on colour and brightness.

pathway.milestone: LCD dominates; OLED desktop monitors and mini-LED backlights are sold for better contrast and HDR
pathway.unlocks: accurate colour and deep blacks for work and entertainment.

pathway.milestone: higher refresh rates and resolutions with faster interfaces
pathway.unlocks: smoother motion for gaming and sharper detail for large screens.

pathway.milestone: microLED and brighter OLED variants at desktop sizes
pathway.unlocks: high brightness without burn-in risk and long lifetimes.

pathway.milestone: flexible and transparent panels at low cost
pathway.unlocks: displays that roll, bend or blend into surfaces rather than sitting on a desk.
